# xUnit.net Cheatsheet


## Project Setup


```bash
# Create test project
dotnet new xunit -n MyProject.Tests

# Add reference to project under test
dotnet add reference ../MyProject/MyProject.csproj

# Add additional packages
dotnet add package Moq              # Mocking
dotnet add package FluentAssertions # Better assertions
```


## Test Attributes


```csharp
// Single test case
[Fact]
public void TestMethod() { }

// Parameterized test
[Theory]
[InlineData(1, 2, 3)]
[InlineData(5, 5, 10)]
public void TestMethod(int a, int b, int expected) { }

// Skip test
[Fact(Skip = "Not implemented yet")]
public void TestMethod() { }

// Categorize test
[Trait("Category", "Unit")]
[Trait("Priority", "High")]
public void TestMethod() { }

// Async test
[Fact]
public async Task TestMethodAsync() { }
```


## Test Data Sources


```csharp
// 1. InlineData - Simple inline values
[Theory]
[InlineData(1, 2, 3)]
[InlineData(5, 5, 10)]
public void Add(int a, int b, int expected) { }

// 2. MemberData - From property or method
public static IEnumerable<object[]> TestData =>
    new List<object[]> {
        new object[] { 1, 2, 3 },
        new object[] { 5, 5, 10 }
    };

[Theory]
[MemberData(nameof(TestData))]
public void Add(int a, int b, int expected) { }

// 3. ClassData - From separate class
public class TestDataClass : IEnumerable<object[]>
{
    public IEnumerator<object[]> GetEnumerator()
    {
        yield return new object[] { 1, 2, 3 };
        yield return new object[] { 5, 5, 10 };
    }
    IEnumerator IEnumerable.GetEnumerator() => GetEnumerator();
}

[Theory]
[ClassData(typeof(TestDataClass))]
public void Add(int a, int b, int expected) { }
```


## Common Assertions


### Equality

```csharp
Assert.Equal(expected, actual);
Assert.NotEqual(expected, actual);
Assert.StrictEqual(expected, actual);  // Reference equality

// With tolerance
Assert.Equal(3.14, 3.1416, precision: 2);

// String comparison
Assert.Equal("hello", "HELLO", ignoreCase: true);
```


### Boolean

```csharp
Assert.True(condition);
Assert.False(condition);
```


### Null

```csharp
Assert.Null(obj);
Assert.NotNull(obj);
```


### Collections

```csharp
Assert.Contains(item, collection);
Assert.DoesNotContain(item, collection);
Assert.Empty(collection);
Assert.NotEmpty(collection);
Assert.Single(collection);  // Exactly one element
Assert.Collection(collection,
    item => Assert.Equal(1, item),
    item => Assert.Equal(2, item)
);
```


### Strings

```csharp
Assert.StartsWith("prefix", str);
Assert.EndsWith("suffix", str);
Assert.Contains("substring", str);
Assert.Matches(@"\d{3}-\d{4}", str);  // Regex
```


### Types

```csharp
Assert.IsType<string>(obj);
Assert.IsNotType<int>(obj);
Assert.IsAssignableFrom<IEnumerable>(obj);
```


### Ranges

```csharp
Assert.InRange(value, low, high);
Assert.NotInRange(value, low, high);
```


### Exceptions

```csharp
Assert.Throws<DivideByZeroException>(() => method());
Assert.ThrowsAny<Exception>(() => method());

// With message validation
var ex = Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => method());
Assert.Equal("Expected message", ex.Message);
```


## AAA Pattern (Arrange-Act-Assert)


```csharp
[Fact]
public void TestMethod()
{
    // Arrange - Setup test data & dependencies
    var sut = new SystemUnderTest();
    var input = "test";
    
    // Act - Execute the method being tested
    var result = sut.Method(input);
    
    // Assert - Verify the result
    Assert.Equal("expected", result);
}
```


## Fixtures (Setup & Teardown)


### Per-Test Fixture

```csharp
public class MyTests : IDisposable
{
    private readonly MyClass _sut;
    
    // Runs BEFORE each test
    public MyTests()
    {
        _sut = new MyClass();
    }
    
    // Runs AFTER each test
    public void Dispose()
    {
        // Cleanup
    }
    
    [Fact]
    public void Test1() { }
    
    [Fact]
    public void Test2() { }
}

// Execution: Constructor → Test1 → Dispose
//            Constructor → Test2 → Dispose
```


### Class Fixture (Shared in One Test Class)

```csharp
public class DatabaseFixture : IDisposable
{
    public string Connection { get; }
    
    public DatabaseFixture()
    {
        // Expensive setup (once)
        Connection = "connection_string";
    }
    
    public void Dispose()
    {
        // Cleanup (once)
    }
}

public class MyTests : IClassFixture<DatabaseFixture>
{
    private readonly DatabaseFixture _fixture;
    
    public MyTests(DatabaseFixture fixture)
    {
        _fixture = fixture;
    }
    
    [Fact]
    public void Test1() { }
    
    [Fact]
    public void Test2() { }
}

// Execution: DatabaseFixture Constructor
//            → Test1
//            → Test2
//            → DatabaseFixture Dispose
```


### Collection Fixture (Shared Across Multiple Test Classes)

```csharp
// 1. Define fixture
public class SharedResourceFixture : IDisposable
{
    public string Resource { get; }
    public SharedResourceFixture() { /* setup */ }
    public void Dispose() { /* cleanup */ }
}

// 2. Define collection
[CollectionDefinition("Shared collection")]
public class SharedCollection : ICollectionFixture<SharedResourceFixture> { }

// 3. Use in test classes
[Collection("Shared collection")]
public class TestClass1
{
    private readonly SharedResourceFixture _fixture;
    public TestClass1(SharedResourceFixture fixture) 
    { 
        _fixture = fixture; 
    }
    
    [Fact] public void Test1() { }
}

[Collection("Shared collection")]
public class TestClass2
{
    private readonly SharedResourceFixture _fixture;
    public TestClass2(SharedResourceFixture fixture) 
    { 
        _fixture = fixture; 
    }
    
    [Fact] public void Test2() { }
}
```


## Test Output


```csharp
public class MyTests
{
    private readonly ITestOutputHelper _output;
    
    public MyTests(ITestOutputHelper output)
    {
        _output = output;
    }
    
    [Fact]
    public void TestWithOutput()
    {
        _output.WriteLine("Debug information");
        _output.WriteLine($"Value: {someValue}");
    }
}
```


## Async Tests


```csharp
[Fact]
public async Task AsyncTest()
{
    var result = await SomeAsyncMethod();
    Assert.Equal(expected, result);
}

[Theory]
[InlineData(1)]
[InlineData(2)]
public async Task AsyncTheoryTest(int value)
{
    var result = await SomeAsyncMethod(value);
    Assert.NotNull(result);
}
```


## Running Tests


```bash
# Run all tests
dotnet test

# Detailed output
dotnet test --logger "console;verbosity=detailed"

# Filter tests
dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~MyTests"
dotnet test --filter "DisplayName~Add"
dotnet test --filter "Category=Unit"

# Run specific test
dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~MyTests.TestMethod"

# Watch mode (auto re-run)
dotnet watch test

# Code coverage
dotnet test /p:CollectCoverage=true
```


## Test Naming Convention


```
Pattern: MethodName_Scenario_ExpectedBehavior

✓ Good Examples:
  Add_TwoPositiveNumbers_ReturnsSum
  Divide_ByZero_ThrowsException
  GetUser_InvalidId_ReturnsNull
  SaveUser_ValidUser_ReturnsSavedUser

✗ Bad Examples:
  TestAdd
  Test1
  AddTest
  MyTest
```


## Project Structure


```
Solution/
├── MyProject/
│   ├── MyProject.csproj
│   └── Calculator.cs
│
└── MyProject.Tests/
    ├── MyProject.Tests.csproj
    ├── CalculatorTests.cs
    └── Fixtures/
        └── DatabaseFixture.cs

Naming Convention:
  Project: MyProject.Tests
  Test Class: ClassNameTests
  Test Method: MethodName_Scenario_Expected
```


## Quick Setup Template


```csharp
using Xunit;

namespace MyProject.Tests;

public class MyClassTests
{
    [Fact]
    public void MethodName_Scenario_ExpectedResult()
    {
        // Arrange
        var sut = new MyClass();
        
        // Act
        var result = sut.Method();
        
        // Assert
        Assert.NotNull(result);
    }
}
```


## Comparison Table


```
┌────────────────────┬──────────────┬─────────────────────┐
│ Feature            │ Syntax       │ Use When            │
├────────────────────┼──────────────┼─────────────────────┤
│ Single test        │ [Fact]       │ One test case       │
│ Multiple inputs    │ [Theory]     │ Same test, diff data│
│ Inline data        │ [InlineData] │ Simple values       │
│ Complex data       │ [MemberData] │ Complex objects     │
│ Reusable data      │ [ClassData]  │ Share across tests  │
│ Per-test setup     │ Constructor  │ Fresh state/test    │
│ Shared setup       │ IClassFixture│ Expensive setup     │
│ Multi-class shared │ ICollection  │ Share across classes│
└────────────────────┴──────────────┴─────────────────────┘
```


## Common Patterns


### Testing Exceptions

```csharp
[Fact]
public void Method_InvalidInput_ThrowsException()
{
    Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => Method(null));
}
```


### Testing Async Exceptions

```csharp
[Fact]
public async Task Method_InvalidInput_ThrowsException()
{
    await Assert.ThrowsAsync<ArgumentException>(
        async () => await MethodAsync(null)
    );
}
```


### Testing Multiple Scenarios

```csharp
[Theory]
[InlineData(0)]
[InlineData(-1)]
[InlineData(int.MinValue)]
public void Method_InvalidInputs_ThrowsException(int input)
{
    Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => Method(input));
}
```


### Testing Private Methods

```
Don't test private methods directly.
Instead:
  1. Test through public methods
  2. If needed, make method internal and use:
     [assembly: InternalsVisibleTo("MyProject.Tests")]
```

## Memory Aid


```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  xUnit Testing Workflow             │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1. [Fact] or [Theory]              │
│  2. Arrange (setup)                 │
│  3. Act (execute)                   │
│  4. Assert (verify)                 │
│  5. dotnet test (run)               │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘

Test Lifecycle:
  Constructor → Test → Dispose
  (New instance per test!)

Shared Resources:
  IClassFixture      → One test class
  ICollectionFixture → Multiple test classes
```


## Quick Checklist


```
✓ Test method name describes scenario
✓ One Assert per test (or closely related asserts)
✓ Tests are independent (can run in any order)
✓ Tests are repeatable (same result every time)
✓ Tests are fast (< 1 second)
✓ No logic in tests (no if/for/while)
✓ Use AAA pattern
✓ Test both happy path and edge cases
```
